text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.66% today, a modest gain that reverses some of the sharp 4% decline from the prior three trading days. The stock is bouncing after oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude recovered slightly to $96.41 a barrel following last week's 8% plunge when Iran-U.S. diplomatic talks raised hopes for de-escalation. However, that optimism evaporated on September 26 when Trump rejected Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal and signaled renewed military action after midterm elections, removing a near-term peace premium from the market.

The refiner benefits from moderately tight supply conditions: U.S. refineries are running at 94% capacity, and gasoline and diesel inventories remain at relatively low levels, which supports margins on fuel sales. But the geopolitical overhang—escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and ongoing attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure—keeps crude prices volatile and prevents the kind of sustained recovery that would drive the stock higher.
